topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The opening connects the lecture to the histopathology practicals and outlines its learning goals.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how research into tumor-causing viruses established that cancer can originate from altered normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental testing of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how experimental assays establish whether a gene or mutation gives cells transformed properties.

topics.label: Cancer gene functions and the effects of mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer mutations are classified by their functional effects and why their behavior depends on the affected protein and pathway.

topics.label: Genetic instability and defective DNA repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the contrasting forms of genetic instability through the DNA repair defects that produce them.

topics.label: Genetic instability from replication and mitotic errors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how failures to faithfully copy and distribute the genome during cell division generate instability that can promote tumor adaptation.

topics.label: Mutation order in colorectal cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how the timing of mutation acquisition, especially the onset of genetic instability, influences colorectal tumor progression.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition and BRCA2 restoration
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics follow inherited tumor suppressor defects from increased cancer susceptibility to a BRCA2 example showing that the resulting repair deficiency need not persist for malignancy to continue.

topics.label: Further reading, questions, and lecture close
topics.groupedBecause: The closing returns to the learning outcomes, offers further reading and questions, and previews the next lecture.
